test_title: SSC CGL 2021 Tier-I (Held On : 21 April 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain a grammatical error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

They ordered the whole area / to be disinfected / on the earliest.
solution:
The correct answer is **'on the earliest'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The erroneous part of the given sentence is '**on the earliest'**.
 
• **On **is a preposition of time used with dates and named days of the week.
 
• **Earliest **implies an end point of time. Hence, the **preposition 'on' **cannot be used with it. 
 
• The correct preposition to be used here is '**at'. **
 
• **'At the earliest'** is a phrase that is** used to indicate the earliest possible time when something will happen or be done.**
 
 
• For Example - The job will not be finished until next year **at the earliest.**
 
 
 
• Thus, **option 4** is the correct answer. 

***Correct sentence - ****They ordered, "the whole area / to be disinfected / **at the earliest"__.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**The prepositions of time - **

 
• **“At” **is used in reference to specific times on the clock or points of time in the day. - *The train arrives at 3:30.*
 
• 
 **“In”** usually refers to period of time. - *I was born in 1986.*
 
 
• 
 **“On”** is used with dates and named days of the week. - *She's working on Monday.*
 
 
• 
 **"By"** is used specifically with an end point of time and it means no later than. - *The show should be finished by 9pm.*
